questions.q: The velocity of the bullet becomes one third after it penetrates $4$ cm in a wooden block. Assuming that bullet is facing a constant resistance during its motion in the block. The bullet stops completely after travelling at \left(4 + x\right)cm$ inside the block. The value of $x$ is$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the given information for the first& $4$ cm,~$u = {v}_{0}$~and~$v = \dfrac{v0}{3}$. Applying equation of motion for constant acceleration,

$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{v0}{3}\right)2 = v^{2} + 2a\left(4\right) ⇒ a = - \dfrac{8{v0}^{2}}{9\left(8\right)} = - \dfrac{{v}_{0}2}{9}$

When the body stops,~$v = 0$

$⇒ 0 = {v0}^{2} + 2a \left(4 + x\right)$

$⇒ {v0}^{2} = 2 \left(\dfrac{{v}_{0}2}{9}\right) \left($4 + x\right)$

$⇒ 4 . 5 = 4 + x$

$⇒ x = 0 . 5cm$

$

questions.q: A vehicle travels $4$ km with speed of $3kmh^{- 1}$ and another $4$ km with speed of $5kmh^{- 1}$, then its average speed is :

questions.solution:
Average speed in this case is given by,& $\dfrac{2}{vav} = \dfrac{1}{v1} + \dfrac{1}{v2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{vav} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{vav} = \dfrac{8}{15}$

$⇒ {v}_{av} = \dfrac{15}{4} = 3 . 75kmh^{- 1}$

questions.q: A ball is thrown up vertically with a certain velocity so that, it reaches a maximum height $h$. Find the ratio of the times in which it is at height $\dfrac{h}{3}$ while going up and coming down respectively.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum height of a projectile thrown vertically upward is given by,& $h = \dfrac{u2}{2g}$.

$⇒ u = \sqrt{2gh}$

Using equation of motion with constant acceleration,

$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{h}{3} = \sqrt{2gh}t - \dfrac{1}{2}gt^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{gt^{2}}{2} - \sqrt{2ght} + \dfrac{h}{3} = 0$

Solving the above quadratic equation we will get the times~${t}_{1}$~and~${t}_{2}$.~$⇒ \dfrac{t2}{t1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2gh} + \sqrt{2gh - 4 \times \dfrac{g}{2} \times \dfrac{h}{3}}}{\sqrt{2gh} - \sqrt{2gh - 4 \times \dfrac{g}{2} \times \dfrac{h}{3}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2gh} + \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}}{\sqrt{2gh} - \sqrt{\dfrac{4gh}{3}}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}$

Thus, the ratio~$\dfrac{t1}{t2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3} + \sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: The position of a particle related to time is given by $x = ( 5t^{2} - 4t + 5 ) m$. The magnitude of velocity of the particle at $t = 2$ s will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that

$x = 5t^{2} - 4t + 5$

The velocity is given by~

$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d ( 5t^{2} - 4t + 5 )}{dt} = 10t - 4$

At~$t = 2s$,

$v = 10 ( 2 ) - 4 = 16ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A body starts moving from rest with constant acceleration covers displacement ${S}_{1}$ in first $( p - 1 )$ seconds and ${S}_{2}$ in first $p$ seconds. The displacement ${S}_{1} + {S}_{2}$ will be made in time :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the displacement ${S}_{1}$ of the body, it can be written that

${S}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}a ( p - 1{)}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

And, for the displacement ${S}_{2}$ of the body, it follows that

${S}_{2} = $\dfrac{1}{2}$a ( p{)}^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

If $t$ be the required time, it follows that

${S}_{1} + {S}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} . . . \left(3\right)$

Equations (1), (2) and (3) imply that

$( p - 1{)}^{2} + p^{2} = t^{2} ⇒ t = $\sqrt{2p^{2} - 2p + 1}$s

$

questions.q: A ball is released from a height $h$. If ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$ be the time required to complete first half and second half of the distance respectively. Then, choose the correct relation between ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

As the body is dropped from a certain height& $h$, its initial velocity will be zero.

For first half,~${h}_{1} = \dfrac{h}{2}$.

Using second equation of motion,~$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

We have,~$\dfrac{h}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{1}^{2}$.

Time taken in travel first half of the height,~${t}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}} . . . \left(1\right)$.

For total height $h$, using again second equation of motion,

$h = $\dfrac{1}{2}$g \left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right)2 ⇒ \left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) = $\sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} . . . \left($2\right)$

From equation~ \left($1\right)$~and~ \left($2\right)$,~

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{t1}{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}}

$⇒ 1 + $\dfrac{t2}{t1} = \sqrt{2}

$⇒ $\dfrac{t1}{t2} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} - 1}

Thus, the relation is~${t}_{2} = $\$left(\sqrt{2} -1\right){t}_{1}$.

$

questions.q: As shown in the figure, a particle is moving with constant speed $\pims^{- 1}$. Considering its motion from~$A$ to $B$, the magnitude of the average velocity is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The given data is&

$v = \pims^{- 1}$

By using trigonometric ratios in the triangle shown above the displacement can be found out by

$sin60 ° = \dfrac{AB}{2R} ⇒ AB = R\sqrt{3}$

The formula for distance is~

$d = vt ⇒ t = \dfrac{d}{v} ⇒ t = \dfrac{120 °}{360 °} \times \dfrac{2\piR}{π} = \dfrac{2R}{3}$

So, the average velocity is~

${v}_{avg} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}R}{\dfrac{2R}{3}} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$= 1 . 5\sqrt{3}ms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : A truck and a car moving with same kinetic energy are brought to rest by applying breaks which provide equal retarding forces. Both come to rest in equal distance.

Statement II : A car moving towards east takes a turn and moves towards north, the speed remains unchanged. The acceleration of the car is zero.

In the light of given statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and Statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done in stopping the car and the truck can be written as

$\begin{cases}W & = & Fx \\ & = & ∆ KE\end{cases}$

As both the car and the truck are moving initially with the same kinetic energy, after being stopped, they will have the same change of kinetic energy.

Also, they are stopped with the same applied force.

Hence, from the above equation, it can be written that~they have the same displacement, i.e.,~${x}_{1} = {x}_{2}$.

Acceleration is a vector quantity. As the direction of motion of the car is different in the two given situations, the acceleration of the car will not be the same.

As the slope of displacement-time is~positive constant in first half and negative constant in second half, so the velocity will be uniform positive and uniform negative value.

$( C - III )$

(D) Here, the slope~$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = constant$.

As the slope of displacement-time is~positive constant, so the velocity will be uniform positive value.

questions.q: When a ball is dropped into a lake from a height $4 . 9m$ above the water level, it hits the water with a velocity $v$ and then sinks to the bottom with the constant velocity $v$. It reaches the bottom of the lake $4 . 0s$ after it is dropped. The approximate depth of the lake is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using& $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

Initially,~$u = 0$, so time taken to reach from~$A$~to~$B$~is $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 4 . 9}{9 . 8}} = 1s$

Now, using~$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$, we have

$v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 9 . 8 \times 4 . 9} = 9 . 8ms^{- 1}$~

$∵ {t}_{2} = \left(4 - 1\right)s = 3s$

$∴ d = {t}_{2} \times v = 3 \times 9 . 8 = 29 . 4m$

questions.q: A ball of mass $0 . 5kg$ is dropped from the height of $10m$. The height, at which the magnitude of velocity becomes equal to the magnitude of acceleration due to gravity, is _____~$m$. [Use $g = 10ms^{- 2}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Consider downward direction to be positive.

Applying first equation of motion,& $v = u + at$

$⇒ v = 0 + gt ⇒ g = gt ⇒ t = 1s$~

Distance covered in~$1s$,~$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}g \times {1}^{2} = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5m$

Hence, height of the point from the surface~$= \left(10 - 5\right)m = 5m$

questions.q: A particle of mass $10g$moves in a straight line with retardation $2x,$~where~$x$~is the displacement in $SI$ units. Its loss of kinetic energy for above displacement is~\left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right)- nJ .$~The value of~$n$~will be~________ .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration can be written as,& $a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$.

Given:~$a = - 2x$(-ve sign is due to retardation)

Therefore,

$v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = - 2x ⇒ vdv = \left(- 2x\right)dx$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left({v}_f^{2} - {v}_i^{2}\right) = - 2\left(\dfrac{x2}{2}\right) = x^{2} ⇒ \left|\dfrac{1}{2}m\left({v}_f^{2} - {v}_i^{2}\right)\right| = mx^{2}$

$⇒ | \Delta KE | = 0 . 01x^{2} = \left(\dfrac{10}{x}\right)- 2$

Hence,~$n = 2$.

questions.q: The displacement and the increase in the velocity of a moving particle in the time interval of $t$ to $( t + 1 ) s$ are $125m$ and $50ms^{- 1}$, respectively. The distance travelled by the particle in $( t + 2{)}^{th}s$ is ___________ $m$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Considering acceleration is constant, we can write

$v = u + at$

As increase in velocity in $1s$ is given as $50ms^{- 1}$, therefore

$⇒ a = 50ms^{- 2}$

Now, displacement covered between given time interval is,

$125 = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

$⇒ 125 = u + \dfrac{a}{2}$

$⇒ u = 100ms^{- 1}$

Velocity after $1s$ will be, $v = 100 + 50 = 150ms^{- 1}$

Therefore, displacement covered in \left(t + 1\right)s\text{to}\left(t + 2\right)s$ will

$∴ Sn^{th} = vt^{'} + \dfrac{1}{2}a\left(t^{'}\right)2, \text{where}t^{'} = 1s$

$= 175m$

$
